Cardiopulmonary Resuscitation (CPR) According to the American Heart Association (AHA), immediate CPR can double or triple chances of survival after cardiac arrest. For untrained bystanders, Hands-Only CPR is recommended: push hard and fast in the center of the chest at a rate of 100 to 120 compressions per minute (to the beat of Stayin Alive). Ensure emergency services are called immediately. Rescue breaths should only be performed by those trained to do so.

[doc14] Drowning First Aid
Drowning First Aid Safely remove the victim from the water without endangering yourself. If unresponsive and not breathing, begin CPR immediately, prioritizing rescue breaths along with chest compressions, because hypoxia is the primary cause of cardiac arrest in drowning cases.

[doc2] Choking (Heimlich Maneuver)
Choking (Heimlich Maneuver) The American Red Cross advises the 5-and-5 approach for choking adults and older children: deliver 5 back blows followed by 5 abdominal thrusts (the Heimlich maneuver). For infants, use 5 gentle back blows followed by 5 chest thrusts while supporting the head and neck. Never perform blind finger sweeps, as this can push the obstructing object deeper into the airway.
